body:
Closes #2195

Formats C floating point values in f-strings with `PyOS_double_to_string()` instead of building a Python float and calling `PyObject_Format()` on it.

Only two shapes are handled in C: an empty format spec, which `str()` reproduces exactly via the `'r'` format character, and a plain precision such as `.2f`, `.3e` or `.4g`. Everything else (alignment, padding, sign, `%`, thousands separators) still goes through `PyObject_Format()`.

Timings on CPython 3.14, arm64, 200k iterations, best of 15:

```
f"{x}"                  161 -> 157 ns
f"{x:.2f}"               63 ->  37 ns
f"... {i} ... {x:.3e}"  127 ->  92 ns
```

The empty spec is not faster since CPython already routes it straight to `repr`, it just avoids the intermediate float object.

Checked the output against Python's own `format()` over 12023 values (random bit patterns, inf, nan, +-0.0, subnormals) times 6 format specs with no mismatches

comment_data.body:
`isdigit` might not be strict enough here. Try `f"{v:.²f}"` which would be a runtime error in Python and current Cython, but I think the `int(precision)` would fail at compile-time here.

Arguably failing at compile-time would be perfectly reasonable, but ideally it should be a "nice" failure.

The simplest fix is probably `precision.isascii() and precision.isdigit()`

Fixed with isascii(). I went with falling back to PyObject_Format rather than a compile-time error, so `f"{v:.²f}"` now raises the same ValueError Python does instead of a traceback out of the compiler

The same pattern already crashes master for integers: `f"{i:²}"` reaches int(prefix) in CIntLike._parse_format. Fixed that line too since it is the same two words, happy to split it out if you would rather keep this PR to floats

comment_data.body:
I think you want to use `.isdecimal()` here.
```python
>>> '٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩'.isdecimal()
True
>>> int('٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩')
123456789
>>> float('٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩')
123456789.0
>>> f'{1.5:٠٩.4}'
'      1.5'
```
https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.isdecimal

comment_data.body:
It seems a bit wasteful to format all variants, then collect them in a dict, and then pick just the one that's relevant for the test. But it's simple and (shallowly) tests a bit more. Why not.

But if we do it this way, then there's no need for cutting off the '%' before the lookup below. Just pass it as is, then it's clear that we are mapping '%' formats to f-strings here. You can also include the `%r` in that case, because why not. And you can add a test that the actual %-formatting (i.e. `fmt % value`), which gets opaquely evaluated by Python's `str` type, gives the same result as Cython's f-string.

commit.message: Format C floats in f-strings without a Python float object
Fix f-string format spec parsing for bare format chars and non-ASCII digits
Use isdecimal() when parsing numeric format specs
Add CPython's float formatting test cases
Key the float test cases by their % format

Apply minor suggestions from code review

Co-authored-by: scoder <stefan_ml@behnel.de>

- more thread safety
- smaller modules, more shared code
- remove Py3.8 support, keep Py3.9+
